subject: economics
title: Other Elasticities: PES, YED, XED
welcome_lead: Beyond PED - supply, income and cross-price elasticities.
meta_desc: A-Level Elasticity: PES, YED and XED applications.
final_note: Different elasticities answer different strategic questions.

concepts.def: Percent change in quantity supplied / percent change in price.
Percent change in quantity demanded / percent change in income.
Percent change in demand for A / percent change in price of B.
XED greater than 0; complements have XED less than 0.

walkthroughs.body_html: PES is higher when firms have spare capacity, mobile inputs and long time horizons. Agriculture is short-run inelastic - harvests take time.
YED greater than 1 marks luxuries (foreign holidays); 0 to 1 marks normal goods (bread); negative marks inferiors (instant noodles). Predicts which sectors boom in growth and shrink in recession.

XED reveals substitutes and complements. Strong negative XED between razors and razor blades; strong positive between Pepsi and Coke. Marketers use these to design bundles and counter rival promotions.
